wth.text: Karn, the silver golem, rescues young Gerrard Capashen from the Phyrexian raids on Benalia and brings him to Sidar Kondo, who adopts him.
Years later Vuel steals the Legacy and deactivates Karn with the Touchstone, after Karn had been tricked into killing an innocent man and had taken his vow of pacifism.
Gerrard reactivates him, and Karn says that although he would give his life to protect Gerrard, his conscience will not let him take another's.

When the Weatherlight planeshifts to Rath and is ambushed by the Predator, Karn is taken hostage and tortured in Volrath's Stronghold, refusing to kill his torturers until the rescue party frees him; he then returns with the Legacy pieces after persuading the Sliver Queen.

tmp.text: Karn is frozen by his own conscience and, as he puts it, does not resist as moggs carry him to the Predator, because Vuel had already deactivated him and stolen the Legacy artifacts.
On Rath the Predator attacks, Gerrard is thrown overboard, and Karn and Tahngarth are captured, where Volrath tells Karn he has failed Gerrard and the Legacy.
Gerrard later reanimates the frozen Karn, who convinces the Sliver Queen to release the Legacy once Hanna understands how the hive mind works.

usg.text: Urza and Barrin build Karn as a silver golem and give him sentience with Xantcha's heartstone, so that he can serve as a probe sent back in time, since natural bodies would not survive the temporal stresses.
Jhoira takes Karn away from Teferi's harassment and names him, a Thran word for mighty, before Urza brands him with a glyph affirming his role.

When Kerrick steals powerstones and the Phyrexians attack, Karn uses Urza's time machine to save Jhoira, but the machine fails, causing the Tolarian Temporal Disaster that destroys the academy; Karn rescues survivors while Urza and Barrin escape.
Later Karn returns with Urza and Barrin to rebuild Tolaria and finds Jhoira alive and Teferi trapped in a slow-time bubble.

ulg.text: The Touchstone deactivates Karn, who stands as a statue for eleven years until Gerrard reactivates him and takes the Touchstone from his hand.
Karn explains that he first only observed, but found that without investment in others, life serves no purpose.
In the end the Legacy Weapon is fired with Urza's stones, Karn's body and Gerrard's life, and Karn, infused with Urza's spark, takes up his master's staff and leaves Dominaria.

uds.text: When the Phyrexians launch a preemptive strike on the project sites, killing thousands including Sisay's parents, Karn carries the surviving Gerrard to Jamuura.

inv.text: Karn confronts Tsabo Tavoc in Koilos, where his memories return, and he helps Gerrard beat her until she retreats to Phyrexia.
He also touches Darigaaz's mind so that the dragon comes to his senses, and Darigaaz kills himself out of horror.
Using the Thran Tome, Karn rebuilds the Weatherlight and gives it sentience, and then Gerrard places Urza's powerstone eyes in Karn's chest, completing the Legacy.
Gerrard, Urza and Karn merge, Yawgmoth is destroyed, and Karn returns as the first artificial planeswalker containing Gerrard and Urza.

apc.text: Urza has Gerrard place his powerstone eyes in Karn's chest, completing the Legacy, and its light eradicates Yawgmoth's essence while Gerrard and Urza die and Karn becomes a planeswalker.

Earlier, Greven's moggs had looted the Legacy artifacts, including Karn, who refused to fight when taken to witness Tahngarth's mutation, until the rescue party freed him and he claimed the Legacy pieces from the Sliver Queen.
A year later Karn, as an accumulation of the Legacy, takes Orim to Mercadia, after taking up Urza's staff and leaving Dominaria.

scg.text: Karn returns to Otaria to take Jeska to Argentum, telling her she is a planeswalker and asking her to travel the multiverse with him.
There he shows Jeska Memnarch, the golem he forged from the Mirari.

mrd.text: Karn creates the plane Argentum from desolate space, forging the Mirari into the sentient Memnarch as its protector.
He leaves Argentum to train Jeska and leaves Memnarch in control, but a drop of Phyrexian oil he left behind infects Memnarch, who becomes addicted to blinkmoth serum and blocks Karn from the plane.
After Memnarch's defeat, Karn restores the dead and returns the kidnapped inhabitants in the Vanishing, leaving the Mirari in the care of Glissa, Slobad and Geth.

dst.text: Karn puts Memnarch in charge of the plane and the palace is named Galdroon.
The infected Karn later retreats to the core, where the Panopticon becomes his throne and then a prison, while Memnarch strains for a vision of Karn.

5dn.text: Karn tells Slobad that saving his friends would cost both of them the spark, and Slobad agrees.
When Memnarch dies, Karn returns, restores the souls in the Vanishing, destroys Memnarch's body and gives the Mirari to Glissa, Slobad and Geth, with Geth becoming its guardian.

tsp.text: Karn creates Argentum, turns the Mirari into Memnarch, and finds himself locked out of Mirrodin after contact with his glistening oil transforms the world.
He travels back in time to seal the Tolarian rift, with Venser's help, and gives up his spark, leaving him vulnerable to Phyrexian oil.
Karn then flees to Mirrodin unknowingly carrying that oil, and he disappears.

fut.text: Karn enters the Tolaria rift and returns to the moment before Barrin's spell, sealing the rift before it opens, and is lost.
Jeska returns to Dominaria seeking vengeance for Karn.

som.text: Karn gave up his spark to heal the Tolarian time rift and wound up on Mirrodin, a world he created, where Phyrexians seized him, since he unknowingly carried Phyrexian oil in his heartstone.
The Phyrexian civilization grew from the corruption inside him, and the Apostles groom him on a throne, acting as jailers when he is lucid.
Imprisoned in the core, he vacillates between raging against captivity and embracing his throne as the new Father of Machines.
At the core Melira cleanses his body, and Venser donates his spark and heart to Karn, who reignites, regains his memories and vows to stop the Phyrexians.

mbs.text: Karn retreats to Mirrodin's Core and is worshipped as the new Father of Machines, held captive by the praetors.
As Phyrexian contagion corrodes his body, the praetors whisper psalms to corrupt his mind, and he is trapped battling the role they force on him.
Venser gives his life and spark to Karn, who is released from Phyrexian tyranny and asks the group to lead the resistance with Melira.

nph.text: Alone in the silent throne room, Karn wonders who he is, while Half-His-Mind says he will become the new Father of Machines.

Warned that the Mirrans are organizing, he barks the word "Offense!", which the Phyrexians take as the order to begin the war on the surface, and he then whispers that he has committed the gravest offense.
Koth finds Karn imprisoned in the Seedcore but must leave him, until the Resistance heals Karn through Venser's sacrifice.

dmu.text: Karn opens a sealed Thran workshop and finds a diagram of the sylex, then tears free a living Phyrexian cable, causing a cave-in, and follows the tunnel to the Phyrexian staging ground where Sheoldred hangs suspended.
He defeats Rona but refuses to kill her, saying he is not a weapon, learns from Sheoldred that sleeper agents hide in every land, and is buried when Rona collapses the cavern onto him.

Ajani digs him out months later, and Karn and Ajani warn the summit leaders that the Phyrexians have returned, though they are met with doubt until Benalish knights burst open into Phyrexian monsters.
Karn deceives the Phyrexians about the sylex's location, and Stenn is revealed as a sleeper agent whom Karn dismembers.

On the Weatherlight, Karn proposes forcing the Phyrexians into open war, and he reconciles with Jhoira, who plans a self-destruct for the Mana Rig, but Ajani is later revealed as a sleeper agent who takes Karn to New Phyrexia.

mat.text: Karn, Kaya, Koth, Melira and Teferi perform a ritual to un-compleat Ajani and Nissa, in which Melira dies and Karn sacrifices his spark.
Afterward Karn holds the beast Nissa fails to summon until it can be studied, as the group settles in Zhalfir.
